description: Advanced Language practice, challenge and test replacement items; authored templates contextualized by day.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, Which inference is logically equivalent to saying that not every reviewed claim was supported?
options: All unsupported claims were reviewed.
At least one reviewed claim lacked support.
No reviewed claims had support.
Every reviewed claim lacked support.
practice.explanation: Not all A are B entails at least one A is not B.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, The memorandum states that some committee members questioned the interpretation. Which conclusion follows?
options: A majority necessarily opposed the interpretation.
Only committee members could question it.
At least one member questioned it, but the text does not tell us whether most members did.
Every member questioned it.
practice.explanation: Some is existential, not a claim about a majority or exclusivity.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, Neither the director nor the researchers responsible for verification ___ willing to certify the result.
options: was
is
has been
were
practice.explanation: The plural subject nearest the verb is researchers, so were is required.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, Which version correctly joins two independent clauses using a conjunctive adverb?
options: The evidence was limited; consequently, the panel postponed judgment.
The evidence was limited, consequently, the panel postponed judgment.
The evidence was limited; consequently the panel postponed judgment.
The evidence was limited consequently; the panel postponed judgment.
practice.explanation: A semicolon joins the clauses and a comma follows the conjunctive adverb.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, Which choice specifically means that the committee revised the conclusion but left all other sections unchanged?
options: The committee revised the only conclusion.
The committee revised only the conclusion.
Only the committee revised the conclusion.
The committee only revised the conclusion.
practice.explanation: Placing only directly before its focus identifies what was revised.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, Which revision clearly makes the researcher the person who inspected the results?
options: The researcher reported a discrepancy after she inspected it.
The discrepancy, having been inspected, was reported by the researcher.
Having inspected the results, the researcher reported a discrepancy.
Having inspected the results, a discrepancy was reported.
practice.explanation: The agent of the introductory participial phrase is the following subject.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, Which verb sequence describes an unreal possibility in the present?
options: If the researcher had been available, the evidence will be checked yesterday.
If the researcher will be available, the evidence would have been checked.
If the researcher were available, the evidence had been checked last week.
If the researcher were available, the evidence could be checked today.
practice.explanation: Were with could expresses a hypothetical present condition and matching consequence.

practice.text: In the astronomical modeling practice scenario, A license remains valid unless annual verification fails. Which claim preserves that conditional meaning?
options: If annual verification does not fail, the license remains valid.
Verification failure guarantees the license always remains valid.
A license is valid only during a year with no verification.
Every verification failure automatically proves a past license was never valid.
practice.explanation: Unless can mean if not; the exception does not establish every consequence when verification fails.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, A survey of volunteers supports a proposal. Which finding would most reduce concern about sampling bias?
options: The questionnaire is distributed in more colorful envelopes.
The original author repeats the survey's conclusion.
A comparable randomly selected sample produces similar responses.
The volunteers report greater confidence in their views.
challenge.explanation: A randomly selected comparison addresses whether the volunteer group differs systematically from the population.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, An average increased after a program. Which inference remains unjustified?
options: The group's mean increased.
Some values could have stayed constant.
Changes in the distribution cannot be inferred from the average alone.
Every individual's outcome necessarily improved.
challenge.explanation: A rising mean does not imply an increase for each individual.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Two indicators change together. Which statement is most defensible?
options: An association is observed, but causal direction and confounding remain untested.
One indicator must have caused the other.
There can be no common underlying influence.
Correlation demonstrates that the measurements are inaccurate.
challenge.explanation: An association alone cannot identify causation or exclude third variables.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Which sentence both concedes a drawback and offers a relevant rebuttal?
options: Implementation is expensive, proving that it is beneficial.
Although implementation is costly, measured long-term savings may justify a limited trial.
The proposal is costly; therefore no one should examine its possible benefits.
The proposal has no drawbacks, so opponents must be irrational.
challenge.explanation: A sound concession acknowledges cost and replies using evidence relevant to the objection.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Every approved study passed ethical review. A study passed ethical review. What follows?
options: Ethical review was unnecessary.
No approved study passed ethical review.
Approval is possible but not established by the ethical review alone.
The study must have been approved.
challenge.explanation: Passing a necessary stage does not guarantee the subsequent outcome.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Only the researchers who supplied raw data were eligible for certification. What must be true?
options: Every raw-data supplier was certified.
Researchers without certification supplied no data.
All eligible researchers received certification.
Every certified researcher supplied raw data.
challenge.explanation: Only sets a necessary condition for certification; it does not guarantee that eligible people were certified.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Which sentence uses whom as the object of a verb in formal written English?
options: Whom did the editor consult before publishing the report?
Whom concluded that the evidence was incomplete?
The reviewer whom presented the findings disagreed.
Whom is responsible for the final decision?
challenge.explanation: Whom functions as the direct object of consult; the other constructions require who.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, The statement 'Mira told Elena that her interpretation was incomplete' is ambiguous. Which revision unambiguously assigns ownership to Elena?
options: Mira spoke to Elena about her incomplete interpretation.
Mira told Elena that Elena's interpretation was incomplete.
Mira told Elena that her interpretation was incomplete.
Her interpretation was incomplete when Mira spoke to Elena.
challenge.explanation: Repeating Elena's name identifies whose interpretation was being assessed.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Which claim most accurately reports a limited observational result?
options: Every apparent improvement was caused entirely by the intervention.
Because improvement occurred, further observation is unnecessary.
Under the conditions studied, the intervention was associated with a measurable improvement.
The intervention always produces improvement in every setting.
challenge.explanation: A bounded claim avoids extending limited observations to a universal causal law.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, Which evidence would independently corroborate a disputed account?
options: The original narrator repeats the event in another paragraph.
A later summary cites only the disputed account.
A reviewer describes the narrative as compelling.
A separately preserved contemporary record confirms the same event.
challenge.explanation: Independent records strengthen corroboration because they do not merely repeat the original source.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, A policy has potential benefits and meaningful uncertainty. Which recommendation best integrates both?
options: Run a bounded pilot with predefined measures before considering wider adoption.
Adopt it universally before collecting data.
Reject it permanently because uncertainty exists.
Accept only outcomes that support the initial proposal.
challenge.explanation: A bounded pilot can test a promising approach while limiting risk and allowing revision.

challenge.text: In the astronomical modeling challenge scenario, A second explanation fits the same findings as the first. Which response most improves the argument?
options: Treat matching observations as proof that only one explanation exists.
Identify a measurement that could distinguish the two explanations.
Discard the alternative because the initial account was stated first.
Use stronger adjectives to make the first explanation convincing.
challenge.explanation: A discriminating test can differentiate hypotheses that currently explain the same observations.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which comparison is logically parallel?
options: The revised report's conclusion is more cautious than the earlier research team.
The revised report's conclusion is more cautious than the university.
The revised report's conclusion is more cautious than the author of the first study.
The revised report's conclusion is more cautious than that of the earlier report.
test.explanation: That refers to the earlier conclusion, so the two compared entities are alike.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which sentence keeps all three complements grammatically parallel?
options: The reviewers agreed to examine assumptions, evaluate evidence, and revise conclusions.
The reviewers agreed to examine assumptions, evaluating evidence, and a revision of conclusions.
The reviewers agreed to examination of assumptions, evaluate evidence, and revised conclusions.
The reviewers agreed to examining assumptions, evaluation of evidence, and conclusions revised.
test.explanation: Examine, evaluate, and revise are parallel verbs under the shared infinitive.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which punctuation correctly introduces an explanatory list after a complete clause?
options: The report evaluated three issues, reliability: validity, and replicability.
The report evaluated three issues: reliability, validity, and replicability.
The report evaluated: three issues, reliability, validity, and replicability.
The report evaluated three issues; reliability, validity, and replicability.
test.explanation: A colon introduces a list when preceded by an independent clause.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which version expresses an unreal past possibility with correct verb forms?
options: If the records will survive, historians might have reconstructed it.
If the records survived tomorrow, historians had reconstructed it.
Had the records survived, historians might have reconstructed the chronology.
Had the records survive, historians reconstructed the chronology.
test.explanation: Past-perfect inversion and modal perfect form a grammatical unreal-past conditional.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, If acceptance requires review, and review requires documented consent, what follows?
options: Consent alone guarantees acceptance.
Every consent form results in review.
A rejected study could not have had consent.
Acceptance is impossible without documented consent.
test.explanation: Necessary conditions chain: acceptance requires review, which requires consent.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which finding best supports generalization beyond an initially narrow, self-selected sample?
options: Comparable results in independently selected, diverse samples.
Greater enthusiasm among the original participants.
More repetitions of the original survey on the same respondents.
An increase in the number of pages of the original report.
test.explanation: Independent sampling and replication address external validity and selection bias.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which conclusion most carefully handles a promising finding and an unresolved alternative explanation?
options: The finding demonstrates that the alternative explanation is impossible.
The finding supports further testing, but the alternative must be evaluated before a causal claim is established.
The observation immediately invalidates every alternative.
No interpretation can be offered until all uncertainty disappears.
test.explanation: This balances provisional support with an untested competing explanation.

test.text: In the astronomical modeling test scenario, Which evidence most directly establishes whether a source's conclusion follows from its data?
options: The number of citations without examining their relevance.
The emotional appeal of the concluding paragraph.
A transparent account of measurements, assumptions, and possible competing interpretations.
The author's professional biography alone.
test.explanation: Transparent methods and logical connections between evidence and claims allow evaluation of validity.
